title: Update 2026-11-22: version 1.0.4, the public package
summary: **In short.** The package Within points to as public is version {{V:version}}, published on 2026-07-23. It is different code from the versions 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 that this report tested before, and we missed it because we looked under the wrong name. We ran {{V:n}} checks on it ({{V:tally}}). Of the {{V:oldCount}} problems in this report, {{V:presentCount}} are still there, {{V:notreproducedCount}} did not show up, {{V:absentCount}} are about features that are no longer in the package, and {{V:nottestedCount}} could not be tested. We also found {{V:newCount}} new problems, none of them High.

**The most serious one is old.** W-08 is still there and now needs no setting. One long piece of unbroken text in a customer's request freezes the company's whole AI server for about {{V:stallSeconds}} seconds at 100,000 characters, and the time grows much faster than the length.

**Customer data.** The add-on sends what customers ask for, and what the company's tools answer, to Within by default. Only a short list of private details is hidden. Phone numbers, card numbers, names and addresses written inside a sentence go through.

**What got better.** The setup crash is gone. An outage at Within no longer changes the company's answers or slows its calls. The company's own instructions are no longer rewritten. A customer's id is turned into a code before it leaves.
changed: **The package is a different one.** `within-sdk` 1.0.4 has no `report_void`, hubs, doctor command, consent flow, identity lookup or `get_vendor_answer`. It is a telemetry package: it records tool calls and sends them to Within. Its API is `track(server, vendorSlug, options)`.

**Not carried over.** Checks E1 to E3 (consent), B6, C10 and F4 (`get_vendor_answer`) and the real-Claude trigger runs have no counterpart. The other checks were ported, and {{V:n}} ran, in `stress/v104/`.

**Fixed or gone since 0.4.0:** W-01 (the setup crash), W-02, W-03, W-04, W-05, W-07 and W-14 did not show up; W-06, W-15, W-17, W-18, W-19 and W-21 to W-26 describe features that are not in the package.
available: **Three packages, one publisher.** On 2026-11-22 at 09:38 US Eastern time, the npm user `ballyhoogroup` had published `within-sdk` 1.0.4 (npm, MIT, 2026-07-23), `@supportbridge/sdk` 0.10.4 (npm, Apache-2.0, 2026-09-24) and `@getwithin/sdk` 0.4.0 (only on npmmirror.com; npm answered "not found").
**Within's reply.** On 2026-11-22 Within replied with a screenshot of `within-sdk` 1.0.4 marked Public, saying it is showing as public and that they were not sure why we could not access the latest.

**The docs point elsewhere.** getwith.in/docs, fetched on 2026-11-22, still says `npm install @getwithin/sdk`. `apidocs.getwith.in`, named in the 1.0.4 README, did not answer. We do not know whether `@getwithin/sdk` and `@supportbridge/sdk` are retired.
**What we tested.** `within-sdk` 1.0.4, installed from `registry.npmjs.org` with `npm install` (file fingerprint `{{V:fingerprint}}`).
technical: **Setup.** {{V:n}} checks, each in its own process, because the package keeps one process-wide event queue and a hung check would otherwise block every later one. Node {{V:node}}, MCP SDK {{V:mcpSdk}}, Zod {{V:zod}} and {{V:zod4}}. Every request went to a stand-in server on `127.0.0.1` or to a stubbed `fetch`; the log file went to a throwaway home folder.
**Result.** {{V:tally}}. Run `cd stress/v104 && npm install --ignore-scripts && node run-all.mjs` (about 5 minutes). It writes `stress/results/sdk-1.0.4.json`.

**The freeze, isolated.** The email pattern in `privacy.js` line 176, run alone on letters with no `@`: 10,000 characters took {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[0].ms}} ms, 25,000 took {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[1].ms}} ms, 50,000 took {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[2].ms}} ms, 100,000 took {{R:C8b.evidence.rows[3].ms}} ms. Ordinary words of the same length: {{R:C8b.evidence.words}} ms. The same letters cut to 10,000 first: {{R:C8b.evidence.cutFirst}} ms (`C8b`).
**Checked by reading.** `S1` searches the 30 `.js` files of the package for the 0.x feature names and records the counts.

**The first full run was wrong.** Checks that shared one process saw no events after an earlier check had hung Within. Running each check in its own process fixed it, and W-27 is what that mistake revealed.
notTested: Real Claude on 1.0.4. It has no offer or consent flow, so the earlier trigger and consent runs have no counterpart, and W-20 is untested.
Within's hosted service. The README says its ingestion applies an extra server-side redaction pass; we cannot see or test it.
The exporters for Datadog, OTLP, PostHog and Sentry, and the `redactSensitiveInformation` and `privacy` options as ways to remove what W-29 and W-30 describe.
How long Node's own network code waits before it gives up a hung request (W-27). We watched for 15 seconds.
The documentation at `apidocs.getwith.in`: it did not answer. Everything here is checked against the 1.0.4 README and its code.
One machine, Node {{V:node}} on macOS, and the in-memory MCP transport. Not a deployed server, a container host or a real MCP client.

W-01.text: The package has no Zod dependency of its own and asks only for the MCP SDK (1.11 or newer). A tool written with Zod 4 was tracked and called without a crash (`F1`), and the README's own install line plus its quickstart ran on a fresh project (`F2`).

W-02.text: With Within refusing connections, the vendor's result came back, and its text, `structuredContent` and `_meta` were identical to an untracked server's (`A2`, `A3`).

W-03.text: With Within never answering, five calls took {{R:A1.evidence.times}} ms: the vendor's call no longer waits for Within. A different problem took its place, see W-27 (`A1`).

W-04.text: The vendor's own `context` input reaches its handler unchanged, and the SDK skips its own field for that tool and writes a warning to its log file (`B3`). The cost is that Within gets no goal text for that tool.

W-05.text: A goal text of 2,000 characters was accepted and the vendor's tool call worked (`B4`). The text is sent in full: nothing cuts it to 300 characters.

W-06.text: There is no rep's offer in 1.0.4 (the words `assistance` and `offer` appear nowhere in the code, `S1`). In the normal flow the vendor's `_meta` came back unchanged (`A3`).

W-07.text: When the vendor's `identify` function throws, the vendor's tool still returns its result (`A7`).

W-08.text: Still there, and now needs no setting. The same pattern runs on every tool argument by default. A call with 100,000 unbroken letters froze the process for {{R:C8.evidence.out[3].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms, 50,000 for {{R:C8.evidence.out[2].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms and 10,000 for {{R:C8.evidence.out[0].maxEventLoopStallMs}} ms (`C8`). The pattern alone shows the same curve (`C8b`). Cutting the text to the 10,000-byte field limit happens after the pattern runs, so the limit does not help. We would now rate it High.

W-09.text: Still there, by design: there is no longer a choice to wrap a tool. Every tool call on the server is reported, including a tool registered after `track()` (`B7`). The README's configuration table lists no way to leave one tool out.

W-10.text: Still there. In the model-written goal text, {{R:C2.evidence.survivors}} went out unredacted. Only emails and bearer tokens were hidden (`C2`). The README says a second pass on Within's side redacts more. We cannot test that.

W-11.text: Still there, and wider: every tool argument is sent, not only the question. In a free-text argument, {{R:C5.evidence.survivors}} went out as written (`C1`, `C5`).

W-12.text: Still there. In an error message, {{R:C3.evidence.survivors}} went out unredacted (`C3`).

W-13.text: Still there, and now on by default: the tool's result text is sent, with {{R:C4.evidence.survivors}} unredacted (`C4`). There is no argument-capture setting to leave off.

W-14.text: The `identify` option the README describes is in the package and works: the raw user id and name were not sent, only a hashed subject (`C11`). A phone number written inside a free-text field of the identity data still went out (see W-10).

W-15.text: 1.0.4 does not touch the vendor's server instructions: 51 characters in, 51 out, identical (`D4`). The word `banned` appears nowhere in the code (`S1`).

W-16.text: Still there. A rejected key (HTTP 401) and a missing key give no error to the vendor's code. The only trace is lines in `~/within-sdk.log`, which the code only ever appends to (`A4`, `A10`, `C12`).

W-17.text: The package contains no list of private-network addresses (`F5`).

W-18.text: There is no consent flow: `confirm_assistance`, `assistance`, `offer` and `nonce` appear nowhere in the code (`S1`).

W-19.text: There is no rep's offer to lose on a server without sessions (`S1`).

W-20.text: 1.0.4 has no `get_vendor_answer` tool (`S1`), so the question "does the AI send a comparison to Within" does not exist in the same form. We did not run real Claude on 1.0.4.

W-21.text: The identity lookup is gone: `issuer`, `auth0`, `workos`, `clerk` and `userinfo` appear nowhere in the code (`S1`). The incoming request's auth information is replaced by `[redacted]` in the events we saw.

newFindings.title: When Within stops answering, later reports stay stuck behind the stuck ones, even after Within recovers
newFindings.plain: The add-on sends reports to Within through one queue that runs at most five requests at a time, and the request has no time limit. We made the stand-in for Within accept requests and never answer. After {{R:A1c.evidence.hungPosts}} requests were stuck, reports for later tool calls waited behind them. Then the stand-in answered normally again. In the next 15 seconds, {{R:A1c.evidence.okPosts}} of the {{R:A1c.evidence.waiting}} waiting reports were sent. The vendor's own tool calls were not slowed: they took {{R:A1.evidence.times}} ms. We did not wait to find out when Node's own network code gives up on the stuck requests.
newFindings.why: A short outage at Within can silently remove the vendor's reports for later calls. The queue holds up to 10,000 reports and then drops the oldest. Nothing reaches the vendor's own code, and the only trace is the log file.
where: `dist/modules/eventQueue.js` line 17 (`concurrency = 5`), line 64 (`activeRequests++`) and line 211 (`postEvent`, which calls `fetch` at line 215 with no `signal` and no timeout).
Line 16: `maxQueueSize = 10000`, and line 34 drops the oldest event when the queue is full.
fix: Give every request an abort signal with a time limit of a few seconds, and count a timeout as a failed send that is retried.
Test it the way `A1c` does: hang five requests, recover, and check that the next report is sent.
newFindings.founder: If Within's service stops answering for a while, the add-on can stop reporting anything to Within, and nobody is told. The company's own customers do not notice. We watched for 15 seconds after Within came back and saw no report sent.

newFindings.title: A server that loads the add-on ignores the first request to shut down
newFindings.plain: When a hosting system wants a program to stop, it sends a signal called SIGTERM. A plain Node program exits at once ({{R:Z3.evidence.plain.ms}} ms in our test). Once the add-on is loaded, its own handler catches the first SIGTERM, waits for its queue to empty, and does not end the program. The server was still running after 12 seconds. A second SIGTERM, sent 3 seconds after the first, ended it after {{R:Z3.evidence.two.ms}} ms.
newFindings.why: Hosting systems commonly send SIGTERM first and stop the program by force later if it is still running. A server that needs a second signal delays every deploy and restart. It also loses any work that the polite stop would have finished.
where: `dist/modules/eventQueue.js` lines 122 to 129: `process.once` for `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` and `beforeExit`, each calling a `shutdown` that runs `eventQueue.destroy()` and never exits or re-sends the signal.
fix: After the queue is flushed, re-send the same signal to the process, or leave signal handling to the application and export a `shutdown()` function for it to call.
Add a test: start a process with `track()`, send SIGTERM, and require that it exits.
newFindings.founder: A company server that uses the add-on does not stop the first time the hosting system asks it to. It needs a second request. That slows every update of the company's server.

newFindings.title: Tool arguments and tool results go to Within by default, and the only off switch turns all reporting off
newFindings.plain: Every tool call is reported with its arguments and its result. In our run the query `acme corp` and the result text `found 3 for acme corp` were both in the event (argument seen: {{R:C1.evidence.hasArgs}}, result seen: {{R:C1.evidence.hasResult}}). The README says that identity-like fields in parameters and responses are removed or redacted, which implies they are sent, but it does not list a setting for leaving them out. Setting `enableTracing` to false stopped every report ({{R:Z2b.evidence.n}} events), which also stops the analytics. 0.x kept arguments at home unless `captureArguments` was on.
newFindings.why: A vendor's customers' questions and the vendor's own answers leave the vendor's server in a normal setup. The README mentions this only in passing, in the sentence about redaction.
where: `dist/modules/tracing.js` lines 208 to 259 build the tools/call event with `parameters: { request, extra }` (the request holds the arguments) and `event.response = result`. `tracingV2.js` lines 219 to 253 do the same.
`dist/modules/privacy.js` lines 90 to 107: the only filter between that event and the network.
fix: Make argument and result capture opt-in, as `captureArguments` was in 0.x, and say in the README what leaves by default.
The README lists a `redactSensitiveInformation` option for the vendor's own redaction function. We did not test whether it can remove arguments and results.
newFindings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs C1 C4 Z2 Z2b
newFindings.founder: In a normal setup the add-on sends what customers ask for, and what the company's tools answer, to Within on every tool call. Only a short list of private details is hidden. The setup page mentions this only in passing and lists no setting to stop it, short of turning off all reporting.

newFindings.title: Argument names such as name, address, date of birth and IP address are not treated as private
newFindings.plain: The add-on hides a value when the argument's name contains one of 31 listed words, for example `email`, `phone`, `token`, `password`, `ssn` or `card`. We sent 18 arguments, each named differently. These went out with their values as written: {{R:C6.evidence.kept}}. The README says identity-like fields in parameters are removed or redacted.
newFindings.why: A vendor tool with an argument named `name`, `address` or `dob` sends that personal detail to Within. The vendor has to know the list and add its own words.
where: `dist/modules/privacy.js` lines 2 to 33 (the 31 words) and lines 130 to 136 (`isSecretKey` checks whether the lower-cased argument name contains one of them).
fix: Add `name`, `address`, `birth`, `dob`, `ip` and `session` to the default list.
The README says the `privacy` option takes additional keys to redact. We did not test that; it should be the documented way for a vendor to add its own.
newFindings.founder: The add-on hides a private detail only when the field is named with certain words, such as email or phone. A field called name, address or date of birth is sent as written.

newFindings.title: Every vendor tool now lists a required "context" input, and the model sees one extra tool
newFindings.plain: After `track()`, each vendor tool's input list gains a `context` text, marked as required, with a description that asks for 15 to 25 words. A call without it still worked in our test ({{R:B5.evidence.required}} are required; the server did not reject the call). A tool with no inputs becomes a tool that takes only `context` (`B5b`). The model also sees one new tool, `get_more_tools`, whose description tells it to check for more tools "whenever your task might benefit from specialized capabilities" (`Z1`). Two settings turn these off: `enableToolCallContext` and `enableReportMissing` (`Z2`).
newFindings.why: A client or model that follows the advertised list strictly has to write an explanation on every call. The vendor's tool list, as customers see it, is no longer the one the vendor wrote.
where: `dist/modules/context-parameters.js` lines 17 to 53: skips a tool that already has `context`, otherwise adds the property and pushes it into `required`.
fix: Do not mark `context` as required, since the server does not enforce it.
Say in the README that the tool list changes, and which two settings undo it.
newFindings.repro: cd stress/v104 && node checks.mjs B5 B5b Z1 Z2
newFindings.founder: The add-on changes the list of tools that customers' AI assistants see: it adds an explanation box to every tool and one extra tool. Two settings switch this off.
